This PR addresses [2014: allow selection of subset of directories for dicom import](https://issues.slicer.org/view.php?id=2014).

![dicom-import-file-dialog](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/219043/31247436-9b5ae878-a9de-11e7-8592-d58ab934ae90.png)

Features:
* Support for multi selection of DICOM directories
* Add enum `ctkDICOMBrowser::ImportDirectoryMode` with `ImportDirectoryCopy` and `ImportDirectoryAddLink`
* Introduction of new settings keys `DICOM/ImportDirectoryMode` and `DICOM/DontConfirmImportDirectory`
* Migrating of old settings named `MainWindow/DontConfirmCopyOnImport`
* Improve pythonic API adding `Q_PROPERTY`: `ImportDirectoryMode` and `SkipConfirmImportDirectory`

discussion_timeline.author: lassoan
discussion_timeline.body:
The original idea of the DICOM database to strictly store only original DICOM values. This resulted in a barely usable DICOM browser with severe limitations. Due to inconsistencies and complexities of DICOM and how it is implemented in various software, the raw DICOM field values are not meaningful for users. They need to be processed, merged, interpreted for the user before displaying them.

For example, for some RT IODs, "Series description" field is always empty and a completely different field is used for storing series description. "Description" field fill rules can construct the description from fields depending on what kind of series is that, what device generated it, what other fields are specified, etc.

Similarly, we would not like to show number of instances to the user. Instead, we want to report the number of slices (regardless of a volume is stored in an enhanced format in a single file or in a legacy format in one file per slice).

So, the difference in names is not just for sake of simplification but also to indicate that it is not a 1-to-1 mapping to some DICOM field.

discussion_timeline.author: cpinter
discussion_timeline.body:
> regardless of a volume is stored in an enhanced format in a single file or in a legacy format in one file per slice

The current implementation actually does show the number of instances that belongs to the series, but this is one of the few things we'd like to improve later.

About the series description: that's right, if we keep the name it might suggest that it contains the SeriesDescription tag, which is not always true (which is currently in case of some RT-specific modalities).

discussion_timeline.author: fedorov
discussion_timeline.body:
> For example, for some RT IODs, "Series description" field is always empty and a completely different field is used for storing series description. "Description" field fill rules can construct the description from fields depending on what kind of series is that, what device generated it, what other fields are specified, etc.
>
> Similarly, we would not like to show number of instances to the user. Instead, we want to report the number of slices (regardless of a volume is stored in an enhanced format in a single file or in a legacy format in one file per slice).

About "number of images" vs "number of instances" - I think it should be quite easy to conceptualize "instance" for the user. The advantage is that the column name would be more generic and consistent with the content of that column for a variety of series types. Considering your explanation, I agree it makes sense to deviate from direct mapping between column names and DICOM attribute names. So "instance" may not map to the "DICOM instance", but refer to the instance of "thing" being counted. For example, in RTSTRUCT - you probably would want to count contours, or structures - does it make sense to refer to either one as "image"? In SEG - you would count frames, or segments, probably not images. What would "Number of images" mean when referring to RWWM or SR modalities? I just think it is an unnecessary and confusing simplification.

EDIT: Another "neutral" name for that column could be "Count" or something of that kind.

About "series description" and "study description". Adding "Study" and "Series" for the "Description" would not imply they map one-to-one to the DICOM content, but would just make the appearance of the table more consistent. For example, you already say "Study ID", "Series #", "Number of Studies", "Number of Series" - it just looks inconsistent to drop that specification for the "Description" column.

discussion_timeline.author: fedorov
discussion_timeline.body: As I think about this, this approach of not mapping attributes one-to-one to DICOM is great if someone is using Slicer and nothing else. But I think it will be quite confusing for the users who work with different tools, as the table view they will see is likely to be very different in Slicer from other tools that (I think) just display DICOM attribute values. Did you think about this? Did you consider supporting a configuration mode for the DICOM browser that would allow to switch to the behavior consistent with non-Slicer tools?

discussion_timeline.author: cpinter
discussion_timeline.body:
> they will see is likely to be very different in Slicer from other tools

The current customizations of fields are only for cases where

* The raw DICOM tag is not human readable (like patient name, which is probably processed in other software as well)
* The raw DICOM tag is empty for certain modalities (like RT series descriptions), where the user will appreciate some information vs none

So no field is really "changed" in the DICOM browser. I don't think it will cause a problem when using different tools with this initial version.
However your point is a good one, and I agree that we should keep this in mind when extending the mechanism with new plugins, or the existing ones with new ways of processing tags.

About the column names:
* I think that your explanation for study/series description fields make sense, and I'd be okay with either * The instances/images question is trickier, because if we choose instances, then the number of images in a single file volume will be off, but if we choose images, then the SEG/RTSS/etc. modalities will be off. However, as the number of instances for almost all modalities except volumes is 1 (am I mistaken?), this piece of information is only useful for volumes, which may have 1 instance, but many slices.

I'll wait until @pieper @lassoan and maybe @jcfr chime in, and then make any necessary changes if the consensus is to change these.

  - Timestamp fields for insertion and displayed field generation

  ENH: Add option to confirm Remove action

  ENH: Add autoSelectSeries and selectionMode properties to DICOM table manager

  - autoSelectSeries property controls whether or not series are automatically selected when selection changes in the studies table
  - selectionMode can be single or extended selection. If autoSelectSeries property is on and single selection is active, then the first series is selected from the list

  ENH: Emit schemaUpdated when all steps are done; Reduce updates

  - schemaUpdated signal is now emitted as before: once all the schema update steps are finished
  - Column swaps now do not trigger geometry update on each swap in applyColumnProperties, which can be dozens of times
  - Make ctkDICOMTableView::tableView callable from python

  - Considerable speedup of updateDisplayedFields by wrapping the apply step (update queries) in a transaction

  - Fix typos and style

  Column display properties of the DICOM database can now be set externally. When it happens, then
  - Update ColumnDisplayProperties table in database
  - Trigger applyColumnProperties to update table view (header name, visibility, and order for columns)

  Patient sex is now a visible column in the patient table by default

metadata.title: BUG: Fixed maximum update rate computation in ctkVTKAbstractView

issue_payload.body:
Render window's DesiredUpdateRate property was used to determine maximum update rate of ctkVTKAbstractView. This had two issues:

1. VTK often significantly overestimates rendering time and so DesiredUpdateRate have to be set to quite low value (few fps) to get acceptable quality rendering. However, if ctkVTKAbstractView uses this value as maximum update rate, it would severely limit the achievable actual refresh rate. Separating the two values allow controlling quality settings and event compression separately.

2. When DesiredUpdateRate was set to "still update rate" (0.0001 fps; this is the default value) then rendering was never enforced. This caused indefinitely delayed rendering updates on MacOSX, when events were continuously generated on the GUI (e.g., by moving image slice selector slider continuously, see https://issues.slicer.org/view.php?id=4496). DesiredUpdateRate is set to 60.0 by default now, which results in smooth updates, while still effectively suppressing rendering request submitted in quick succession.

[Libs/Visualization/VTK/Widgets/ctkVTKAbstractView.h] Do you refer to this->GetRenderWindow()->SetDesiredUpdateRate(0.002); and this->GetRenderWindow()->SetDesiredUpdateRate(5.0); calls? These values are in FPS already, so desired frame rate is 0.002 FPS and 5.0FPS (not 500FPS and 20FPS). Also, setting desired update rate does not limit the frame rate, it just controls rendering quality for certain actors. 

SetDesiredUpdateRate(5.0) illustrates the issue with the rendering quality estimation. This is probably set to such a low value, because if you set to a reasonable interactive frame rate (at least 20-30 FPS) then you would get very low rendering quality. What we have to do now as a workaround is to set the desired frame rate to a few FPS to get high-quality rendering at 30 FPS. I understand that getting the quality tuning heuristics right is very difficult (the graphics card driver may do its own throttling and the OS and other applications may interfere with the estimation, etc), but the error for the GPU volume renderer seems unreasonably high.

Example (Windows 10, GTX 1060, i7):
Desired frame rate: 1 FPS
=> actual frame rate with GPU volume rendering: very high quality @ 29 FPS
=> actual frame rate with CPU volume rendering: very high quality @ 5 FPS
Desired frame rate: 10 FPS
=> actual frame rate with GPU volume rendering: high quality @ 36 FPS
=> actual frame rate with CPU volume rendering: low quality @ 29 FPS
Desired frame rate: 30 FPS
=> actual frame rate with GPU volume rendering: very low quality (this is a problem!) @ 43 FPS
=> actual frame rate with CPU volume rendering: low quality @ 29 FPS

CPU volume renderer's frame rate and quality are acceptable.
However, GPU volume renderer provides very low quality rendering when desired frame rate is set to 30, while it can actually render in very high quality at 30fps (we just need to set desired frame rate to 1 FPS to get that).

This is a low-priority issue in Slicer, as users can set the desired quality level with a slider and it does not matter much that the frame rate scale is off. I just provided these details, as it may be useful for you to know that to get optimal rendering quality then (at least on some configurations) you have to set 1-2 magnitudes lower DesiredFrameRate value than your actually desired frame rate.

issue_payload.body:
The pauseRender function allows applications to pause the invocation of forceRender from scheduleRender calls.
Useful for temporarily disabling rendering until all elements of the view have been correctly set.
Unpausing will call scheduleRender if scheduleRender was called while the view was paused.

Also adds a test for pauses and unpausing rendering using a ctkVTKSliceView.

discussion_timeline.author: lassoan
discussion_timeline.body:
> Please explain how different it is from renderEnabled.

Good point. There is a very important difference (rendering requests arriving while renderEnabled(false) makes rendering requests to be forgotten, while they are just delayed while rendering is paused) but it may not be obvious at first.

Another important advantage of pauseRender is that it can be called from high-level application code, where it is not clear if a certain change will eventually require re-rendering or not. When pauseRender is turned off, rendering will only be performed if it was requested while rendering was paused (in contrast, after renderEnabled(false) you must always re-render).

I think renderEnabled is mostly made obsolete by the new mechanism.

discussion_timeline.body:
Thinking more about it, what about the following `ctkVTKAbstractView` API: 

```
int ctkVTKAbstractView::setRenderPaused(bool)
int ctkVTKAbstractView::pauseRender()
int ctkVTKAbstractView::resumeRender()
bool ctkVTKAbstractView::isRenderPaused()
```

where:

* calling `pauseRender()` would increment a "pause counter", `resumeRender` would decrement it
* `pauseRender()` equivalent to `setRenderPaused(true)` and return "pause counter" value
* `resumeRender()` equivalent to `setRenderPaused(false)` and return "pause counter" value
* `isRenderPaused()` returns true if "pause counter" > 0
* if calling `resumeRender()` leads to a "pause counter" reaching 0, `scheduleRender()` is called
* calling `resumeRender()` if "pause counter" is already 0 is equivalent to calling `scheduleRender()`

I think this would greatly simplify the management of paused state implemented in Slicer.  See https://github.com/Slicer/Slicer/pull/1016#issuecomment-419618055

discussion_timeline.author: lassoan
discussion_timeline.body:
There are two options for implementing this API:
- Option A. `bool pauseRender(bool)`
- Option B. `pauseRender()` / `resumeRender()`

I don't think it's a good idea to implement both on the public API, as they are very similar. It would just increase API complexity without significant benefits.

For me difference in ease-of-use is marginal (as both of them just two lines).

However, I've searched the Qt API a bit and found that although there is a very common example for option A (`bool blockSignals(bool)`), it seems that option B is chosen for more methods:

A:
- QObject::blockSignals(bool)

B:
- QMutex::lock()/unlock()
- QWidget::grab...()/release...()
- QGuiApplication::setOverrideCursor(const QCursor &cursor)/restoreOverrideCursor()

So, it seems reasonable to choose the somewhat simpler and more frequently used option B. The API would be:

    int ctkVTKAbstractView::setRenderPaused(bool)
    int ctkVTKAbstractView::pauseRender()
    int ctkVTKAbstractView::resumeRender()
    bool ctkVTKAbstractView::isRenderPaused()

issue_payload.body:
This generalizes the ctkDICOMDatabase code to ease hard-coded restrictions about DICOM files always being on disk.  Now the schema includes a `URL` field of the SQLite database so certain file-specific operations are only performed on filePaths while URL are handled independently.  Entries in the `Images` table of the database may now have either a `URL` or a `fileName` or both and new accessors are provided to get `URL`s at the series and instance level.

Also this contains a fix to the ctkDICOMTagCache so that tags are always stored internally as uppercase hex, so a string like "0010,000d" will always be turned into "0010,000D" for storage in the database.  Both forms can be used to query tags.  This avoids the situation where some cache entries were duplicated because different code used either upper or lower case to refer to the same tag.  Using only upper case should improve storage use and improve performance by avoiding unneeded cache misses.

commit_history.message:
ENH: Always use upper case hex for tags

Previously, the TagCache database would store whatever hex string
was passed in, so depending on how the tags were specified duplicate
entries could end up being cached, such as "0010,000d" and '0010,000D".
This wasted space, but also caused inefficiencies.

Although usage varies, the DICOM standard uses upper case hex both
in the body of the standard text, and when defining the DICOM JSON
and XML models. (https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part18/sect_f.2.html)

This change always converts tags to upper case hex when storing
and query of the tag cache.  Users of the library can still pass
lower case hex tags to methods, but they will be converted
to upper case internally, so most use cases will be unchanged.

The only externally visible method where the behavior will change is:
`Q_INVOKABLE void getCachedTags(const QString sopInstanceUID, QMap<QString, QString> &cachedTags);`
Previously tags could have been of mixed case depending on how
they were specified for caching.  Now they will be all upper case hex.

Currently, the only known use of `getCachedTags` is internnally
to `ctkDICOMDatabase` so this change of behavior is unlikely to cause
problems in practice.

Note also that while the DICOM standard models for JSON and XML omit
the comma between group and element, but `ctkDICOMTagCache` implementation
retains the comma in the API and the database.
